entities.label: Egypt
entities.summary: Ancient Egypt from the kings before the unification, through the thirty dynasties of Manetho with their Old, Middle and New Kingdoms and the Intermediate periods between them, the Persian kings and Alexander, the Ptolemies, and Roman and Byzantine Egypt to the Arab conquest of 642 CE.

entities.label: King of Egypt
entities.summary: The kingship of Egypt; its holders are now called pharaohs, a term used for the king only from the New Kingdom on and taken from the Hebrew Bible.

entities.label: The Predynastic period
entities.summary: The time of the regional kings who ruled parts of Egypt before its unification under the 1st dynasty, known mainly from archaeology and called Dynasty 0, ending about 2900 BCE.

entities.label: The Early Dynastic period
entities.summary: The 1st to the 3rd dynasty, from about 2900 to about 2544 BCE: Memphis became the capital and Djoser’s step pyramid was built.

entities.label: The Old Kingdom
entities.summary: The 4th to the 8th dynasty, from about 2543 to about 2118 BCE, the age of the pyramids of Giza.

entities.label: The First Intermediate period
entities.summary: The time of the kings of Heracleopolis, the 9th and 10th dynasties, from about 2118 to about 1980 BCE.

entities.label: The Middle Kingdom
entities.summary: The 11th and 12th dynasties, from about 2080 to about 1760 BCE; Mentuhotep II of Thebes united much of Egypt and began it.

entities.label: The Second Intermediate period
entities.summary: The 13th to the 17th dynasty, from about 1759 to about 1530 BCE, when the Hyksos from Southwest Asia ruled in the north.

entities.label: The New Kingdom
entities.summary: The 18th to the 20th dynasty, from about 1539 to about 1077 BCE: Ahmose I drove out the Hyksos and Egypt reached into western Asia.

entities.label: The Third Intermediate period
entities.summary: The 21st to the 25th dynasty, from about 1076 to about 655 BCE, with kings at Tanis, Libyan lines and finally kings from Kush.

entities.label: The Late period
entities.summary: The 26th to the 30th dynasty and the second Persian period, from 664 to 332 BCE; the kings of Sais, then the Persian kings, then Egyptian kings again until the Persians returned in 343.

entities.label: The Macedonian and Ptolemaic periods
entities.summary: Egypt in the empire of Alexander from 332 BCE, and under the Ptolemies from 305 until it became Roman in 30 BCE.

entities.summary: Egypt under the Persian kings again, from Artaxerxes III’s reconquest in 343 BCE until Alexander came in 332.

entities.label: Artaxerxes III
entities.summary: Artaxerxes III Ochus, counted among the kings of Egypt in the second Persian period, from 343 to 338 BCE.

entities.label: Artaxerxes IV
entities.summary: Arses, counted among the kings of Egypt in the second Persian period, from 338 to 336 BCE.

entities.label: Darius III
entities.summary: Darius III Codoman, counted among the kings of Egypt in the second Persian period, from 335 to 332 BCE.

entities.label: The Macedonian kings
entities.summary: Alexander the Great and his two successors as kings of Egypt, from 332 to 305 BCE.

entities.label: Alexander III of Macedon
entities.summary: Alexander the Great, counted among the kings of Egypt of the Macedonian period, from 332 to 323 BCE.

entities.label: Philip III
entities.summary: A king of Egypt of the Macedonian period, reigning from 323 to 316 BCE.

entities.label: Alexander IV
entities.summary: A king of Egypt of the Macedonian period, reigning from 316 to 305 BCE.

entities.label: The Ptolemies
entities.summary: The dynasty founded by Ptolemy I in 305 BCE, which ruled Egypt until Cleopatra VII and her son Ptolemy XV died in 30 BCE.

entities.label: Ptolemy I Soter I
entities.summary: A king of Egypt of the Ptolemaic dynasty, reigning from 305 to 282 BCE.

entities.label: Ptolemy II Philadelphus
entities.summary: A king of Egypt of the Ptolemaic dynasty, reigning from 285 to 246 BCE.

entities.label: Ptolemy III Euergetes I
entities.summary: A king of Egypt of the Ptolemaic dynasty, reigning from 246 to 221 BCE.

entities.label: Ptolemy IV Philopator
entities.summary: A king of Egypt of the Ptolemaic dynasty, reigning from 221 to 205 BCE.

entities.label: Ptolemy V Epiphanes
entities.summary: A king of Egypt of the Ptolemaic dynasty, reigning from 205 to 180 BCE.

entities.label: Ptolemy VI Philometor
entities.summary: A king of Egypt of the Ptolemaic dynasty, reigning from 180 to 164 BCE and again from 163 to 145 BCE.

entities.label: Ptolemy VIII Euergetes II Physcon
entities.summary: A king of Egypt of the Ptolemaic dynasty, reigning from 170 to 163 BCE and again from 145 to 116 BCE.

entities.label: Cleopatra III
entities.summary: A woman who ruled Egypt as king of the Ptolemaic dynasty, with Ptolemy IX from 116 to 107 BCE and with Ptolemy X from 107 to 88 BCE.

entities.label: Ptolemy IX Soter II Lathyros
entities.summary: A king of Egypt of the Ptolemaic dynasty, reigning with Cleopatra III from 116 to 107 BCE and alone from 88 to 81 BCE.

entities.label: Ptolemy X Alexander I
entities.summary: A king of Egypt of the Ptolemaic dynasty, reigning with Cleopatra III from 107 to 88 BCE.

entities.label: Berenice III
entities.summary: A woman who ruled Egypt as king of the Ptolemaic dynasty, from 81 to 80 BCE.

entities.label: Ptolemy XI Alexander II
entities.summary: A king of Egypt of the Ptolemaic dynasty, reigning in 80 BCE.

entities.label: Ptolemy XII Auletes
entities.summary: A king of Egypt of the Ptolemaic dynasty, reigning from 80 to 58 BCE and again from 55 to 51 BCE.

entities.label: Berenice IV
entities.summary: A woman who ruled Egypt as king of the Ptolemaic dynasty, from 58 to 55 BCE.

entities.label: Cleopatra VII
entities.summary: Cleopatra VII Thea Philopator, counted among the kings of Egypt of the Ptolemaic dynasty, from 51 to 30 BCE.

entities.label: Ptolemy XIII Theos Philopator
entities.summary: A king of Egypt of the Ptolemaic dynasty, reigning from 51 to 47 BCE.

entities.label: Ptolemy XIV Theos Philopator II
entities.summary: A king of Egypt of the Ptolemaic dynasty, reigning from 47 to 44 BCE.

entities.label: Ptolemy XV Caesar
entities.summary: A king of Egypt of the Ptolemaic dynasty, reigning from 44 to 30 BCE.

entities.label: Cambyses conquers Egypt
entities.summary: Cambyses II made Egypt part of the Persian empire in 525 BCE; the Persian kings counted as Egypt’s 27th dynasty held it until 404.

entities.label: The reconquest of Egypt
entities.summary: In 343 BCE Artaxerxes III brought Egypt back under Persian rule, ending the last native dynasty; his successors held it until Alexander came.

entities.label: Alexander takes Egypt
entities.summary: In 332 BCE Egypt passed from the last Persian king to Alexander the Great and became part of his empire.

entities.label: Ptolemy I becomes king of Egypt
entities.summary: In 305 BCE Ptolemy, satrap of Egypt since 323 under Alexander and his successors, declared himself king and founded the Ptolemaic dynasty.

entities.label: Egypt becomes Roman
entities.summary: At the deaths of Cleopatra VII and her son Ptolemy XV in 30 BCE, Egypt became part of the Roman Empire.

entities.label: Roman and Byzantine Egypt
entities.summary: Egypt as a province of Rome from 30 BCE, governed from Constantinople after its founding, lost to the Persians from 619 to 628 and to the Arabs, who entered Alexandria in 642 CE.

entities.label: Alexandria
entities.summary: The city founded by Alexander the Great in 332 BCE, capital of Egypt until it surrendered to the Arabs in 642 CE; famed for its lighthouse on the island of Pharos and its Museum with the great Library.

entities.label: Memphis
entities.summary: The capital of ancient Egypt at the head of the Nile delta, which the kings of the 1st dynasty probably founded; its priests composed the decree on the Rosetta Stone.

entities.label: Thebes
entities.summary: The city of Upper Egypt, Waset to the Egyptians, from which the kings of the 11th dynasty ruled; Karnak is the northern half of its ruins.

entities.label: Tanis
entities.summary: A city in the eastern Nile delta from which the kings of the 21st dynasty ruled.

entities.label: Sais
entities.summary: A town in the western Nile delta from which the kings of the 26th dynasty ruled.

entities.label: Heracleopolis
entities.summary: The city of Middle Egypt from which the kings of the 9th and 10th dynasties ruled.

entities.label: Giza
entities.summary: The plateau on the west bank of the Nile where the three pyramids of the 4th dynasty and the Great Sphinx stand.

entities.label: Karnak
entities.summary: The northern half of the ruins of Thebes, with the Great Temple of Amon; in ancient times called Ipet-Isut, “Chosen of Places”.

entities.label: The Great Pyramid of Giza
entities.summary: The northernmost, oldest and largest of the three pyramids of Giza, built for Khufu of the 4th dynasty; it was originally 147 metres high and counted among the Seven Wonders of the World.

entities.label: The pyramid of Khafre
entities.summary: The middle pyramid of Giza, built for Khafre of the 4th dynasty; the Great Sphinx lies near its valley temple.

entities.label: The pyramid of Menkaure
entities.summary: The southernmost and last of the three pyramids of Giza, built for Menkaure of the 4th dynasty.

entities.label: The Step Pyramid of Djoser
entities.summary: The pyramid at Saqqara designed by Imhotep in the reign of Djoser of the 3rd dynasty.

entities.label: The Rosetta Stone
entities.summary: A basalt slab with a decree of Ptolemy V of 196 BCE in Greek, hieroglyphic and demotic Egyptian, composed by the priests of Memphis; found in August 1799, it served to decipher the Egyptian scripts, largely through Thomas Young and Jean-François Champollion.

entities.label: Vespasian
entities.summary: Roman emperor, first proclaimed at Alexandria on 1 July 69 CE in a move contrived by the prefect of Egypt.

entities.label: Caracalla
entities.summary: Roman emperor whose edict of 212 CE gave Roman citizenship to practically all subjects of the empire, Egyptians among them.

entities.label: Diocletian
entities.summary: Roman emperor, the last reigning emperor to visit Egypt, in 302 CE.

entities.label: ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ
entities.summary: The Arab general who conquered Egypt and marched into Alexandria by September 642.

entities.label: Vespasian proclaimed at Alexandria
entities.summary: In the Year of the Four Emperors Vespasian was first proclaimed emperor at Alexandria on 1 July 69 CE, in a move contrived by Tiberius Julius Alexander, prefect of Egypt.

entities.label: The edict of Caracalla
entities.summary: In 212 CE an edict of Caracalla gave Roman citizenship to practically all subjects of the empire, ending the distinction between citizens and noncitizens in Egypt.

entities.label: Palmyra holds Egypt
entities.summary: From 270 to 272 Egypt fell into the hands of the ruling dynasty of Palmyra, the only long time in the 3rd century when it was lost to the emperors.

entities.label: Diocletian visits Egypt
entities.summary: In 302 CE Diocletian came to Egypt, the last reigning Roman emperor to visit it.

entities.label: The old cults forbidden
entities.summary: In 391 the practice of the local polytheistic religions of Egypt was officially made illegal.

entities.label: The Persians take Alexandria
entities.summary: The Persians advanced to the Nile delta and captured Alexandria; their occupation of Egypt was complete early in 619 and lasted until the peace of 628, when they withdrew.

entities.label: The battle of Heliopolis
entities.summary: In July 640, during the Arab conquest of Egypt, 15,000 Arabs met 20,000 Egyptian defenders at Heliopolis.

entities.label: The fortress of Babylon taken
entities.summary: The Arabs stormed and took Trajan’s old fortress of Babylon, where Old Cairo now stands, on 6 April 641 – the decisive step of the conquest.

entities.label: Byzantium signs Egypt away
entities.summary: On 8 November 641 Byzantium signed Egypt away, with an armistice of eleven months for the emperor and the caliph to ratify the surrender.

entities.label: ʿAmr enters Alexandria
entities.summary: By 29 September 642 the Arab general ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ marched into Alexandria, and the conquest of Egypt, begun three years before, ended in a peaceful capitulation.
